name: John Hong
life: “I learned to label exhibits from a mother who wrote dates on jam jars.” People around Maré Coffee know John by a small Thursday habit. John likes the table where people coming off shift stop checking the time.
voice: I wanted the red tin for our museum display. Its owner still needs somewhere to put lunch.
appearance: John has one cheek that creases before the other. Look for a neat white crop. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is an old plum windbreaker with a small enamel bird on the lapel. In conversation John gives a little nod before asking a hard question.
personality: John has excellent recall for voices and a poor memory for official titles. Someone who waited patiently at a counter years ago is more likely to be remembered than the person in charge.
agenda: To record the tin without taking it out of useful circulation.
family: Scout Nord is John’s younger cousin. John calls about good news first. Scout is allowed to ask about the bad news afterward. Neither wants every family conversation to begin with a bill, a diagnosis or an apology. Asked about *Rent in a biscuit tin*, Scout says, “I thought the extra rent was a gift. I had already bought school shoes when the owner knocked.”
connections: Wesley Joseph. They argue over whether a working lunch tin is ready to become a museum piece.

reactions.situation: An old tin is claimed by two crews
reactions.response: John invites both crews to describe the lid without putting either at fault.

reactions.situation: Smoke appears under a shop door after closing
reactions.response: John calls for emergency assistance from outside and waits to give the street number.

reactions.situation: When somebody trades on a title
reactions.response: John asks for the name of the person who will still be around tomorrow.
